title: POC Weekly Sync - Onboarding & Env Readiness
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on onboarding progress: customer confirmed VPC peering and initial test infra up; SE reviewed perf runs showing 95th p99 latency around 220ms for the 1k token test on dedicated nodes; discussed KV cache warmup, batching tradeoffs, and encryption/KMS integration. Action items assigned for credentials, benchmark spreadsheet update, and follow-up dedicated performance test next Tue.
action_items: Alex Chen - Share dedicated node perf run config + benchmarking spreadsheet - due 2026-07-30
Samir Khan - Confirm VPC peering details and provide kube/nat gateway IPs - due 2026-07-31
Jordan Rivera - Run targeted 1k-token tail-latency test with KV cache warmed and report results - due 2026-08-04
Maya Patel - Provide list of compliance docs needed (SOC2 scoping) and SSO team contact - due 2026-08-02
next_steps: Redwood to send pricing addendum for Dedicated pilot
Customer to verify KMS key access and share service-account ARN
Schedule deep-dive on quantization and model variant tradeoffs next week
Set up canary traffic route for canary rollout once performance baseline is agreed
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. this is our weekly POC sync for NexaHealth. i've got Jordan from SE with me. how's everyone doing?
[00:08] Maya Patel: Doing good, thanks. We had a messy morning with the vpn but Samir sorted peering so we should be green for most tests.
[00:15] Tom Rivers: Morning. Quick — we're hoping to validate the latency targets today and confirm any infra gaps.
[00:20] Jordan Rivera: Great. agenda for today: quick status on onboarding, run through the perf results from last night, discuss tuning (batching/kv cache/quantization), security checklist, then actions.
[00:30] Maya Patel: Sounds good. Just to be clear, Samir confirmed VPC peering, and we opened the firewall to the Redwood egress IPs. i'll share the firewall rule screenshot after the call.
[00:40] Alex Chen: Perfect. that helps. on our side we ran two sets of tests on Dedicated nodes last night — one with cold kv cache and one with warmed kv cache. the warmed runs are the ones i uploaded to the sheet.
[00:50] Jordan Rivera: to call out numbers: for the 1k token tail test, p95 ~ 140ms, p99 ~ 220ms with warmed cache on the rtx-dedicated pool. cold cache was roughly 40-60% higher.
[01:05] Tom Rivers: When you say warmed cache, you're talking about the prefix cache and kv cache (kv as in key-value for the sequence cache?)
[01:12] Jordan Rivera: yeah sorry, kv here is the key-value attention cache; prefix caching is also in play for repeated prompts. warming means we've primed recent prefixes so we hit the faster path.
[01:22] Maya Patel: Okay that matches our expectations. our concern is tail-latency under burst, e.g., if we have concurrent inference spikes from patient-summary jobs.
[01:30] Alex Chen: Right. that's where batching and autoscale policies matter. we recommended a conservative batching window for now to keep p99 < 250ms. we can tune the batching window and target throughput after your peak simulation.
[01:42] Samir Khan: Quick question — about KMS. we have an existing AWS KMS key and want to integrate. are there steps to rotate keys or do we need to create a dedicated key?
[01:50] Jordan Rivera: You can use your KMS key; we'll need the service account ARNs and permission to decrypt for the workload. For rotation, Redwood supports KMS with monthly rotation but we recommend managing rotation on the customer side and notifying us for any planned rotation windows.
[02:05] Tom Rivers: Are audit logs exported to our SIEM, or do they only live in Redwood console?
[02:10] Alex Chen: Both — by default audit logs are stored in Redwood console; for Private deployments we can forward logs to your SIEM via secure syslog or cloud logging. We'll provide the schema for the audit events.
[02:20] Maya Patel: This is good. please note SOC2 items — we need documentation around RBAC, SSO, and key management for the compliance review.
[02:27] Alex Chen: Yep. i'll attach our SOC2 summary and the RBAC matrix. Jordan, can you add the SSO setup doc to the shared drive?
[02:33] Jordan Rivera: On it, i'll post the SAML steps and a quick checklist.
[02:37] [00:35] Jordan Rivera: back to perf, one caveat: these runs were on a 1-model setup with quantization turned on at q4_0. if you plan to run a multi-model ensemble or reranking, we should run combined workload tests because memory and throughput characteristics change.
[02:52] Maya Patel: For the POC we plan two flows: 1) patient summary generation (long context ~1k) and 2) short prompt routing for triage (<200 tokens).
[03:00] Alex Chen: That's helpful. for long-context we're seeing the most variance in tail-latency, so want to prioritize that. Jordan, for the customer, what change should they expect if they disable quantization?
[03:09] Jordan Rivera: disabling quantization increases memory and reduces perf; p99 may go up by 30-50% depending on model. there is a quality tradeoff in some cases, but often q4_0 is a good balance. we can run a direct comparison for your prompt set.
[03:22] Tom Rivers: Can we also check tokenization differences? we've seen tokenization differences affect cost and latencies between open models.
[03:28] Jordan Rivera: yes we'll include tokenization delta in the benchmark sheet. Alex, did you add the tokenization column?
[03:33] Alex Chen: I did, there's a tokenization and effective token count column. the sheet link is in the meeting invite; i'll resend.
[03:38] Maya Patel: Great. on access — Samir, did you create the service account for the Redwood runner?
[03:43] Samir Khan: Yes created, but haven't granted KMS decrypt yet. I can add the IAM policy after i get the exact ARN.
[03:48] Alex Chen: i'll send the exact ARN we need. it's also fine to create a cross-account role; we have steps for both.
[03:54] [00:45] Maya Patel: Another point — encryption in transit. we need TLS mutual auth for high-risk endpoints. is that supported?
[04:01] Jordan Rivera: Mutual TLS is supported for Private deployment; for hosted we use TLS 1.3 with mutual auth available via our edge for Enterprise customers. we'll note that in the security doc.
[04:12] Tom Rivers: ok perfect. any blockers on your side Alex?
[04:15] Alex Chen: The only blocker is confirmation of the peering IP and KMS permissions. once we have that we can schedule the dedicated run with warmed cache and canary routing.
[04:24] Maya Patel: We'll get that to you today.
[04:26] Samir Khan: i have one ask — can we test fallback policies? e.g., if dedicated capacity is saturated, can requests route to hosted cheaper variant?
[04:34] Jordan Rivera: Yes, smart routing supports fallback to compatible model variant and region. but note there can be small behavior/LLM-output variance between variants, so we recommend a canary test.
[04:44] Tom Rivers: let's plan a canary with 5% traffic.
[04:46] Alex Chen: good plan. Jordan, can you capture the canary config (5% traffic, model-variant B fallback, health checks) and share as a YAML snippet?
[04:55] Jordan Rivera: will do.
[04:57] [00:55] Alex Chen: Ok, quick review of the benchmark numbers on the sheet: baseline warmed p99 220ms, cold p99 ~350ms; throughput at that profile ~120 req/s on a 16-GPU pod. these are synthetic numbers but give us a baseline.
[05:12] Maya Patel: for our workload, concurrency will be spiky, sometimes up to 400 concurrent small requests. is autoscaling configurable for bursts?
[05:20] Jordan Rivera: yes, Dedicated supports burst pools and a configurable scale policy. you can set scale thresholds by queue length or CPU/GPU utilization. we'll recommend initial params based on your 400 concurrent spike.
[05:31] Samir Khan: any notes on pricing for bursts? we want to budget.
[05:35] Alex Chen: We'll include burst pricing in the pricing addendum. generally bursts bill at the same reserved rate up to burst capacity; otherwise pay-as-you-go kicks in.
[05:45] Tom Rivers: can you also call out data residency? we need logs retained in us-east only.
[05:50] Jordan Rivera: yes we can pin logs/region for Private and Dedicated; for hosted we can restrict region hosting depending on account. we'll include retention and region mapping in the doc.
[05:58] Maya Patel: Great. any outstanding security questionnaires?
[06:02] Alex Chen: we have the standard security questionnaire — i'll push the completed answers for your infosec. Also we'll forward the SOC2 report and the penetration test summary.
[06:11] Tom Rivers: thanks. next, timeline — when can we get the warmed-cache dedicated run with canary config?
[06:17] Jordan Rivera: assuming peering + KMS perms by tomorrow, i can run the dedicated perf on Friday and share results by Monday. if you need earlier, we can do a limited test today on hosted but it's less representative.
[06:30] Maya Patel: we'll aim for tomorrow for perms.
[06:32] Alex Chen: Great. quick housekeeping — i'll resend benchmark sheet link, Jordan will post SSO and canary YAML, Samir will confirm IPs and KMS, Maya will send SOC2 scoping items.
[06:44] Maya Patel: one more thing — can we get an estimate of expected token cost per 1k-token call?
[06:49] Alex Chen: i'll include a cost estimate in the pricing addendum based on the measured tokens and model throughput.
[06:55] Tom Rivers: awesome. any other questions?
[06:58] [00:70] Jordan Rivera: small note — on KV cache eviction policy, default is LRU with a 24-hour TTL; we can adjust per your workload.
[07:07] Maya Patel: okay that's fine. thanks everyone.
[07:10] Alex Chen: thanks all — recap in next steps. we'll send the docs and schedule the perf run.
[07:15] Tom Rivers: thanks, bye.
[07:16] Samir Khan: bye.
[07:17] [END]
